parsed.explanation: State layer is highly protective: anti-discrimination, hate-crime, M/F/X documents, identity-consistent state custody, and a 2022 care shield for visitors from banning states. Combined regime is capped by operative federal exposures state law does not cancel: binary-sex federal facilities, 2025 passport/entry screening with refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation, federal custody hormone removal/conversion model, and reported forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse in immigration custody. Litigation leaves exact rules uncertain. If outed at a federal checkpoint, facility or detention, consequences can be severe despite state protections.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary-sex definition, X-marker passports not processed, Supreme Court allowed restrictions Nov 2025; entry cable directs refusal where documents/records discrepancy or reasonable doubt on sex, and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation; trans athletes banned from entry to compete; passports confiscated/blocked reported.
entry_documents.protection: State IDs/licences offer M/F/X and change on request, but that is resident-facing and does not control foreign-visitor passports or federal visa adjudication.
entry_documents.interaction: State document openness does not pre-empt federal entry screening; a mismatch can move from refusal to fraud investigation and detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections model from 2026 includes hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State custody since 2018 treats people consistent with gender identity in housing, strip searches, clothing and materials.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: State custody protection applies only in state custody; federal prison and immigration detention remain separate, harsher systems the visitor can enter after a federal encounter.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: 2025 executive order bars use of government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with gender identity; state map shows many bans elsewhere and one transtrespass arrest nationally, illustrating federal/state facility risk.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state is in Most Protective tier with no documented bathroom ban; state anti-discrimination law covers public places and services.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State public-accommodation protection does not cancel bans in federal buildings, military or national facilities within the state.

care_services.exposure: National orders target youth gender-affirming care and proposed federal rules would bar public insurance reimbursement under 18; DOJ subpoenaed hospital records nationally. Several orders blocked/enjoined, status unresolved.
care_services.protection: 2022 state shield law protects patients/providers from civil/criminal liability when care lawful here was banned in home state; conversion therapy on minors banned since 2017.
care_services.interaction: Shield protects state care for a travelling minor/parent, but does not prevent federal investigation, funding or entry consequences.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal government removed gender-identity materials, rescinded prison LGBTQ order, and May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups described as radically pro-transgender; cash-reward memo used radical gender ideology phrase but not as criterion.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crime law covers gender identity/expression, strengthened June 2026 effective Oct 2026; national hate-crime statute also exists.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat-framing increases outing/investigation risk, while state hate-crime and discrimination laws provide local recourse whose enforcement for visitors is not documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal January 2025 order directs criminal investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; federal sports ban could refuse entry to a minor trans athlete; youth-care bans elsewhere affect visiting families.
minors_guardians.protection: State anti-bullying law covers gender identity on all school premises including cyberbullying; 2021 ruling left trans girls' school-sports eligibility intact; shield law relevant to travelling families.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor may be protected at a state school/clinic yet encounter federal school-funding, sports-entry or records investigations through a parent/guardian's federal interaction.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: National poll 2025: 66% supported assigned-sex documents and 69% sports alignment, indicating substantial public support for restrictions; no state-specific visitor violence count documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State discrimination ban in public places, employment and services since 2011, plus hate-crime enhancement, are documented operative protections.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local tolerance/recourse is comparatively strong, but federal policing, immigration detention and national political climate can override street-level safety after an outing.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport and executive-order challenges unresolved; several orders enjoined; ranking is rubric-based not enforcement-based, and no state-specific violence/implmentation data documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have blocked some federal orders, ACLU sued over passports, and state protections are codified, but no documented visitor remedy success is in dossier.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty itself is exposure: traveller cannot reliably predict whether federal screening, facility or care rules will be enforced at the time of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: ward/facility assignment by document marker creates delayed/denied services and reliance on exceptions, without a credible execution pathway. This case is similar or slightly higher because state facilities/custody and shield law are protective, but federal detention abuse is more severe than this anchor.

Lower: that anchor had brief holding, release, apology and compensation with courts reliably ordering release and custody never threatened. Here federal entry can be refused with lifetime-ineligibility consideration and immigration custody abuse is documented, so remedies are weaker at federal level.

Higher: that anchor had routine police stops, passport/phone confiscation, fines and courts deferring to police, deterring travel without usually imprisoning. This combined regime has stronger state protections and no documented routine street stops in this state, though federal custody abuse prevents a 0.65+ rating.

parsed.synthesis: State protections materially reduce everyday exposure in public places, schools, state custody and care, including for minors and travelling families via the shield law. They do not neutralise the federal layer: entry screening based on sex discrepancy, federal facility exclusion, and federal/immigration custody practices create a continuous, potentially severe outing pathway. Interaction is decisive—document mismatch at entry or a federal facility can lead to refusal, investigation or detention where state protections do not apply. Hence a mid-scale rating: protected locally, exposed nationally.
